newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Taiwan futures end easier in line with cash.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Taiwan futures end easier in line with cash.

text.p: The SIMEX MSCI Taiwan stock index futures ended easier on Tuesday in line with profit-taking in Taipei stocks.
Dealers said the new lead May contract looked set to come under further pressure with near-term resistance seen around 360.0, while 350.0 was likely to provide support.
The contract settled at 352.1 against its opening 357.5 on volume of 1,596 lots. April, which expired on Tuesday, settled at 361.5 against 363.0 on 832 lots.
The MSCI Taiwan cash index ended 2.87 points down at 361.59.
"The market looks kind of toppish. I would sell on rallies in the short term but the overall picture is still buoyant," a trader with a local institution said.
Refco (Singapore) Pte Ltd said in a daily commentary the May contract looked set to begin trading at a nine-point discount to the cash index, as the April contract did when it became the spot month.
Refco attributed the fall in Taipei stocks to investor anxiety that corporate earnings would not be high enough to sustain the 24 percent rally in Taiwan's weighted index since January.
Nikkei futures were slightly easier after failing to sustain initial gains by the close of Monday's morning session.
Dealers said volumes were low and trade confined to a narrow range ahead of a Japanese holiday on Tuesday. Interest was expected to remain poor until after Japan's Golden Week break.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract was 90 points lower at 18,560 after hitting a high of 18,680 on volume of 4,420 lots.
The dollar's strong tone after the weekend Group of Seven (G7) nations meeting had little impact on the market, dealers said.
The dollar rose to a high of 127.10 yen in early Tokyo trade due to the absence of any reference to concerns about a weak yen from the G7 meeting.
A trader with a local institution said the June Nikkei showed potential to break below the 18,550 support level but was likely to hold above 18,300.
He said the market looked set to trade within an 18,300-18,750 range for the next few days and a test of the 19,000 target was likely to prove difficult in the absence of fresh news.
The April MSCI Taiwan index contract was at 366.5 at 0250 GMT against an opening 365.5 on volume of 905 lots.
